about: Coach-facing wording Christian has APPROVED for parts of a game the renderer otherwise cannot say: primary-event conditions (register V4-V6) and information rules (V16-V22), and later the modifier criterion and termination (V8c, V8d). His order of 14 October 2026, Step 4 component 3: 'Enable accurate coach-facing communication of scoring conditions and information rules, using approved language.' An entry is used only when it carries approvedBy with who, a date, his words verbatim and the communication standard it was reviewed under; the loader ignores any other entry and a data test fails it. Wording is data, so no sport term enters universal code. Starts EMPTY on 14 October 2026: until he approves a sentence, every such field is withheld and the activity is refused at communication rather than paraphrased. The first entry, A01-W1, was added 18 October 2026 (stage M5): his own sentence for the build-out scoring rule, reply filed 19 October 2026, item 1. A01-W2 and A01-W3 were added 18 October 2026 (design step L14): his reply filed 20 October 2026, item 1 (the pressing team's regain score, our draft approved as written) and item 2 (the building team's scoring eligibility, in his own simplified wording). His approval covers these sentences only: "I understand that the remaining coach-facing sentences are still drafts, so this approval applies specifically to the two scoring statements, not yet to the entire activity." AMENDED 25 October 2026 (P1, his reply filed 28 October 2026, items 3, 4, 5 and 9): A01-W3 now holds his simplified sentence of item 9 ("I approve simplifying the sentence to:" "If the building team loses possession, it cannot score again until the next goalkeeper restart."), its 20 October sentence kept below it as superseded, with his words ("This is a communication simplification, not a change in scoring eligibility."); the template POSSESSION_CONTINUES now holds his item 5 wording ("Each team keeps attacking the same target."), its 19 October sentence kept as superseded; and two template sentences are added, FIRST_BLOCK_CHOICE (item 4, "Decide which team builds first.") and EQUIPMENT (item 3, "One 12 × 6 ft goalkeeper-defended goal, balls, cones or field markers, and two team colors plus a distinct goalkeeper color."). A superseded sentence is never said and never matched: it is the record of what he approved before.

entries.sentence: Building team: Score by carrying the ball beyond the marked line or passing to a teammate who receives it under control beyond the line. The progression must begin with the goalkeeper's build-out and occur before the building team loses possession. Uncontrolled clearances do not score.

approvedBy.quote:
1. Build-out scoring condition — Approved with revised wording
I'd like to simplify the coach-facing wording while preserving the four conditions established in the knowledge.
Suggested wording:
"Building team: Score by carrying the ball beyond the marked line or passing to a teammate who receives it under control beyond the line. The progression must begin with the goalkeeper's build-out and occur before the building team loses possession. Uncontrolled clearances do not score."
A longer pass received under control remains a valid solution.
The important distinction is that the building team's scoring opportunity applies only during an active build-out episode.
approvedBy.ccs: Coach Communication Standard RC2: his own revision of our draft condition sentence, section 4 of our email of 18 October 2026 ("The wording that needs your approval"), which put every sentence to him as a draft

The match values are the game's own, copied from A01 as the checked pathway builds it at 12 and 11 players, identical in both blocks (measured). His 19 October sentence names only the goalkeeper. OUR INFERRED READING: he narrowed his own wording to the one arm this realization builds, after section 4 of our email of 18 October 2026 told him that every build-out in this activity starts with the goalkeeper and the engine cannot yet build the controlled-defensive-restart arm; a test pins that no episode starter of A01 carries a restart kind, so the arm his sentence leaves unnamed cannot occur. The suffixes after ' - ' on the 18.c, 18.f and 19.a asAuthored texts are our glosses, matched here as data only. If any of these values changes, the entry stops matching, the fields are withheld again and A01 is refused at communication (a safe failure).

approvedBy.quote:
1. Pressing team's regain score — Approved as written.

"The pressing team also scores by winning the ball inside that zone, provided it genuinely establishes possession; a contested touch, deflection or loose ball does not count."

This preserves the intended incentive for controlled high regains without requiring an additional pass or dribble.

entries.sentence: If the building team loses possession, it cannot score again until the next goalkeeper restart.

approvedBy.quote:
9. Build-out scoring eligibility
I approve simplifying the sentence to:
"If the building team loses possession, it cannot score again until the next goalkeeper restart."
Because every dead ball now produces a goalkeeper restart, the separate reference to playing the ball out is unnecessary.
This is a communication simplification, not a change in scoring eligibility.

superseded.sentence: If the building team loses possession or plays the ball out, it cannot score again until the next goalkeeper restart.

approvedBy.quote:
2. Building team's scoring eligibility — Include, with simplified wording.

"If the building team loses possession or plays the ball out, it cannot score again until the next goalkeeper restart."

I think this clarification is useful because play continues after turnovers. Coaches should understand that regaining possession does not restore the original build-out scoring opportunity.

entries.note: Added 18 October 2026 (design step L14); his reply filed 20 October 2026, item 2, in HIS wording, which replaces our draft. One sentence for the building team's scoring eligibility, said once, for his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 4 (the scoring instructions must make clear that continuing to attack does not restore the building team's eligibility). It covers what the sentence says and nothing more: the building role's credit bound (B8 = BUILD_OUT_EPISODE, A01-R1-B8-1: its holder scores only inside a build-out episode, which ends when it loses possession - the change of possession, GF2-07.a - or plays the ball out - the restarts after it, A01-R1-T1-5 and T1-7, which A01-R1-T7-3 makes begin another episode - and which only a goalkeeper restart begins, A01-R1-T1-1..3), and the origin condition that names that restart (RPC-001-18.a: its type, its exact scope and its referents, the same values as A01-W1, whose note explains the goalkeeper-only reading of the two arms; a test pins that no episode starter of A01 carries a restart kind). Those episode-ending transitions are not fields an entry can cover (the renderer says them in its own How it works sentences); what this sentence says about them is the B8 episode they end, checked by GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE clauses 4 and 5. The progression, control and exclusion conditions are NOT covered: this sentence does not say them. Two entries covering one field (MEASURED, approved-wording.unit.ts and first-activity-end-to-end.unit.ts): each located entry is said once where all its own covers hold, independently of the other, citing the fields it covers; a field is withheld only where no entry says it. So B8 and the origin's three fields are cited by A01-W1 and by A01-W3, and neither entry decides the other: without A01-W1 the three conditions only it covers are withheld (refused), and without A01-W3 the fields are still said by A01-W1, so a test pins that the served activity says this sentence once. Its place in How to score, straight after A01-W1, follows from citing the building role's bound (render-concrete-game.ts scoringInRoleOrder, then table order). If any of these values changes, the entry stops matching (a safe failure for these fields, which A01-W1 also says). AMENDED 24 October 2026 (R2, the d27 design's section 2.8, the R1 review's should-fix; this note only, his sentence, covers and approval unchanged): the restarts after the ball goes out named above (A01-R1-T1-5 and T1-7, which A01-R1-T7-3 made begin another episode) were withdrawn on 24 October 2026 (R1) by his reply filed 27 October 2026, item 4 ('Whenever the ball becomes dead, play resets to a new goalkeeper-initiated build-out.'); the ball going out is now A01-R1-T1-8 and T1-9, which A01-R1-T7-1 makes begin a new episode, each a goalkeeper restart awarded to the building team. The sentence stays true: under the common restart 'or plays the ball out' is always followed at once by a goalkeeper restart, so that clause gives the coach nothing further to apply; it is flagged for him (the design offers to shorten it), never edited here. AMENDED 25 October 2026 (P1; his reply filed 28 October 2026, item 9: "I approve simplifying the sentence to:" "If the building team loses possession, it cannot score again until the next goalkeeper restart." "This is a communication simplification, not a change in scoring eligibility."): the sentence is now his simplified one, and the one this note describes above is kept in superseded with its 20 October approval. The covers are unchanged and so is what the sentence covers: the building role's credit bound and the origin condition. The episode a ball going out ends is still ended, by the goalkeeper restart that follows it (A01-R1-T1-8, T1-9, A01-R1-T7-1), as above; the sentence simply no longer names that moment, which the How it works sentence says (every dead ball is a goalkeeper restart). No game value changes.
